meta.title: Khmer A1 Beginner
meta.subtitle: 500 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Khmer is the language of Cambodia. Both study directions in one deck: Khmer → English (see the Khmer, recall the meaning) and English → Khmer (see an English meaning, recall the Khmer). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 500 words for a beginner, aligned to A1 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand and use familiar everyday expressions and very basic phrases aimed at the satisfaction of needs of a concrete type' — a learner here is able to introduce themselves and others, to ask and answer questions about personal details such as where they live, people they know and things they have, and to interact in a simple way provided the other person talks slowly and clearly and is prepared to help. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: no exam board publishes a graded word list for Khmer, so this deck is not any examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 387 of the 500 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — greetings and the polite yes of a man and of a woman, introducing yourself, family and the words for older and younger, numbers and the classifiers they are counted with, telling the time, days and months, food and drink, shopping and money, the home, the town and getting about, the body and feeling ill, the weather, colours, and the pronouns, question words, prepositions and conjunctions every sentence is built out of — and the other 113 are the commonest remaining words of Khmer, counted in the articles of the Khmer Wikipedia. The first day's greetings come first and the rest are dealt by that count, so the words you meet most often come early; an encyclopaedia's commonest words lean towards the written language. Every headword is printed in Khmer script with Wiktionary's romanisation beneath it, a phonetic spelling that shows the vowel each letter's series gives it (ក with ា is kaa, គ with ា is kiə) — the Khmer Alphabet deck, the first in this collection, teaches the script and the two series. There are no forms to learn: Khmer words never change shape. Real example sentences come with 348 of the 500 words, three apiece for 212 of them — the sources hold few Khmer sentences — with the word picked out in colour. There is no speaker button, since few devices have a Khmer voice. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings, romanisation and some example sentences: English Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0), via the kaikki.org extraction and the entries' own pages. Frequency: the Khmer Wikipedia, the dump of 1 November 2026 (CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
